title: fix(plugin-audit): the parent-record read gate writes one branch per parent object the read names, not one per registered object
body:
Fixes #24060

Clause-②: no

The gated read answers the same row set through fewer OR branches: no export, no schema change, no accept-set change.

## What changed

The parent-record read gate (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/parent-record-read-gate.ts`) ANDs one branch per parent object into every non-system read of `sys_activity`, `sys_audit_log` and `sys_comment`. It enumerated every registered parent object, whatever the read asked for. It now intersects that enumeration with the read's own `object_name` filter (ADR-0139 D4):

- **`namedParentObjects(where)`** reads the parents a `where` confines its rows to: `object_name` as a plain value, `{ $eq: V }` or `{ $in: [V, ...] }`, each the only key of its comparand and every `V` a machine name, at the root or inside a root `$and` at any depth. Several confinements intersect. Anything else is passed over: an `$or`, a `$not`, any other operator, a comparand with two operators, a value that is not a machine name (another case, a number). A passed-over conjunct can only narrow the rows further, so the set stays an over-approximation of the parents the rows name. Values are held to the machine-name spelling because two distinct machine names compare unequal under every collation and coercion a driver applies; another spelling might not.
- **`enumerateParentObjects(engine, gate, where)`** keeps only the named parents when the read names any. `planParentReads` hands it `ctx.ast.where` as the read reached the gate, so the `ReadableIds` leaves and the bounded probe's parents (D5 classes 2 and 3) shrink together. A probe whose classes hold no named parent is not run.
- **Unchanged:** the ledger's outside class (rows about no record) is still ORed in whole; the audit-capability exemption is still decided first; the three whole-read probes (delegated caller, engine that cannot classify, no `canReadObject`) still scan the caller's own `where`; a read with no confinement keeps every branch.

### A second producer of the same class, fixed in place: the withheld-update rule

Measurement showed most of the statement comes from a sibling in the same package. `computeWithheldUpdateFilter` (`activity-field-redaction.ts`, ADR-0139 E6) writes one `keptRowsOfParent` branch per parent of the gate's own enumeration (`enumerateParentObjects(engine, ACTIVITY_GATE)`), with one `$contains` per served field in each, and narrowed only to a single `$eq` pin. In the fixture below it is 2,326 of the 2,629 bindings. It now hands `ast.where` to the same enumeration, so it narrows exactly as the gate does.

To keep its verdict identical on every row the read can match, one thing is still asked of the full enumeration: whether the rule narrows the read at all. When no named parent gets a field answer, the remaining parents are asked (security-service calls only, no SQL; before this change every non-pinned read asked all of them). If one is narrowed, the named parents are kept whole, and a read naming no enumerated parent gets the rule's own deny sentinel, which is what the full set of branches selected on that read. If none is narrowed, there is no filter, as before.

This file is outside the claim's declared file surface (`parent-record-read-gate.ts` and the callers' hand-in). It is taken under the bounded in-place rule: the same defect class (a per-parent expansion that ignores the read's own filter), mechanical (one argument to the shared enumeration, plus the decision above), no other claim on the file per the claim's serial-constraint note (no open PR touches `plugin-audit` source), and the same test family. The landing site stays in `@objectstack/plugin-audit`.

## Measured

A scratch harness (not committed): real `ObjectKernel`, `ObjectQLPlugin` and `AuditPlugin`, `SqliteWasmDriver` in memory, 148 registered objects (140 harness objects with 8 text fields each, plus the platform objects the plugins register), and a security stand-in answering `canReadObject`, `getReadFilter`, `getReadableFields` and `getQueryableFields`. A member reads `sys_activity` with `where: { object_name: { $in: [3 objects] } }`, newest first, `limit: 20`, then counts it. Statements were captured through knex's `query` event.

| run | rows statement | count statement | probe pre-scans |
|---|---|---|---|
| base `b0fe9fad4` | 711.8 KB, 2,629 bindings | 711.8 KB, 2,628 bindings | 2 |
| this branch | 14.9 KB, 60 bindings | 14.9 KB, 59 bindings | 0 |
| base, field answers withdrawn (withheld rule inert, gate alone) | 17.4 KB, 303 bindings | 17.4 KB, 302 bindings | 2 |
| this branch, same | 0.6 KB, 12 bindings | 0.5 KB, 11 bindings | 0 |

Rows served 20, total 30, on both trees. The bytes-per-binding ratio of the card's statement (396 KB over 1,402 bindings, about 289) matches the base run with the withheld rule live (about 277), not the gate alone (about 59), so the second producer is very likely most of the card's statement too. The card's control-plane case itself was not re-measured here: NOT MEASURED, reason: no control-plane boot in this container.

## Pins

- **Branch count** (`activity-read-visibility.test.ts`): a read for 3 objects of 40 registered carries exactly 3 branches, one leaf per named parent; the same engine's unfiltered read carries 40.
- **The shapes it reads**: plain value, `$eq`, `$in`, nested root `$and`, two intersecting confinements, an `$in` beside a root `$or`.
- **A named object the gate does not enumerate** (unregistered, audit-excluded, the stream itself) gets no branch; naming none, an empty `$in`, or two contradicting pins is the deny-all sentinel.
- **Unread shapes keep the full enumeration**: 13 shapes (`$or`, `$not`, `$nin`, `$ne`, mixed-operator comparands, a non-machine-name value, a number in `$in`, `$startsWith`, an `$in` on another column, a non-array `$and`), each 40 branches.
- **The probe**: a read naming a middleware-narrowed parent pre-scans that parent only (not the federated one); a read naming neither runs no pre-scan and reads no parent. A delegated caller's whole-read probe is unchanged.
- **The ledger** (`audit-log-read-visibility.test.ts`): a named read keeps the named parent's leaf and the outside class beside it; naming no enumerated parent leaves the outside class alone, never the deny-all sentinel.
- **The withheld rule** (`activity-withheld-update.integration.test.ts`, unit block): an `$in` read is judged against the named parents alone; with no answer for the named parents the full enumeration still decides (kept whole, the deny sentinel, or no filter).
- **Identity on a real engine and driver**: `parent-record-read-leaf.integration.test.ts` reads `{ object_name: { $in: [doc, vault, gated] } }` and the same filter spelled as an `$or` of equalities (which the gate does not read, so it keeps every branch) for two members and the admin. A member reads its own doc and gated records and not the vault; the admin reads all three. Row ids and totals are identical across the two spellings and equal the ground truth. The narrowed read carries 3 branches (doc leaf, vault leaf, gated probe) against the full enumeration's. `activity-withheld-update.integration.test.ts` does the same across the withheld rule's member and admin, and the withheld update stays withheld from the member.

## Ablation (once)

The fix was committed first. `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` deleted the one line in `enumerateParentObjects` that drops a parent the read does not name (anchor hits 1 to 0; blob `ba05a61b0b0b` to `bc1640a1f1d4`; an on-disk `grep -c` read 0 during the run). It then ran the four pinned files: **8 failed, 106 passed**. The branch-count pin read `expected [ …(40) ] to have a length of 3 but got 40`, and the shape, deny-all, probe, ledger, both withheld-rule and the leaf-integration pins went red. The identity pins that compare against the `$or` spelling stayed green, as they should, because both spellings run through the full enumeration. Restore: `git checkout HEAD`, blob back to `ba05a61b0b0b` equal to HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` empty (the tool's own proof, then `git status --porcelain` clean). No build leg: the pins import the gate from `src` by relative path, so nothing is resolved through `dist`.

## Tests and gates (head `c19fb3c6e`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: **55 files, 891 tests passed** (run at `2b7f3abd0`. The only later commits are the changeset and a merge of `origin/main`, which touches nothing in this package).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit typecheck` (`tsc`, scripts tsconfig, `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0, `0 file(s) / 0 error(s)` held in the test-typecheck debt ledger.
- Derived gate families (`dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, 65): 63 exit 0. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `pnpm check:i18n` are NOT MEASURED locally: PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3), because they read the built output of packages this worktree did not build. CI runs both. `dispatch-gates --ran`: `65 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 63 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED`. The repo-wide scans are CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **ADR-0139 D4** says the gate writes one branch per enumerated parent. This narrows the enumeration per read without changing what any read selects. The withheld rule's single-pin narrowing in the same package is the precedent. No ADR amendment is proposed. A reviewer who reads D4 as fixing the enumeration per gate rather than per read should say so.
- **Failure modes narrow.** A leaf or probe for an object the read does not name is no longer composed or run. A composition refusal (D3) or a failing pre-scan for such an object therefore no longer fails or denies a named read. On a driver that refuses the leaf, a read that names only objects the gate does not enumerate now answers empty, where it answered the D3 refusal. The neighbour card #23980 is not addressed here.
- **Comments narrow too**, through the shared `computeParentRecordFilter`, with no comment-specific pin (the shared function is pinned through the activity and ledger callers). The `comment-access-hooks.ts` header still says one branch per registered parent object. That is accurate for an unfiltered read, and the header is outside the claim's surface, so it is not edited.
- **Two readers of `object_name` now live in one package.** `pinnedParentObject` (the query guard's single-equality pin, which also drives the withheld rule's pinned path) and `namedParentObjects` (set-valued, the gate's). They answer different questions for different consumers, so they are not merged here.
- **The HTTP door was not exercised.** The console bell sends `$filter: { object_name: { $in: roster } }` (objectui `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/sharedUserFeeds.ts`), and the protocol door hands the engine the lowered object form, so the shape the gate reads is the one it gets. No REST boot measured it: NOT MEASURED, reason: reasoning from the two doors' code, not a request.

- **Seat's append, from the dev's report (read-only, dormant, not filed):** the module header of `parent-record-read-gate.ts` says the probe excludes rows about an object this gate does not enumerate. That holds for the restricted probe only. The whole-read probe (delegated caller, no `canReadObject`, an engine that cannot classify) has no enumeration, so it keeps any machine-name parent. No producer of rows about a non-enumerated registered object was measured.
